title: Sandustry Mods — Workshop Status, Safety & Where to Watch (EA)
description: Sandustry mods overview for Steam Early Access: what is confirmed from official channels, Workshop uncertainty, safe community watching, and FAQ — no invented mod lists.
note: Early Access tooling and store features can change. This page does not invent Workshop listings, mod APIs, install steps, or “best mods” tables. Re-check Steam news and official Discord before trusting any third-party installer.

paragraphs: Searchers looking for sandustry mods usually want Steam Workshop support, a community mod list, or install instructions for unofficial packs.
Sandustry is a dig-and-automate factory sandbox from Lantto Games, published by Hooded Horse, sold as Steam Early Access (app 2764460) with a separate free demo (app 3490390).
This fan page answers the search intent honestly: what official sources currently support saying — and what they do not.
Preferred sources for this wiki are the Steam store pages, the Hooded Horse Sandustry official wiki, and the official Discord / YouTube / Reddit communities linked from Steam.
Public store marketing for Sandustry centers on destructible sand physics, refining, conveyors, filters, fluids, and a growing Early Access content roadmap — not a documented first-party modding SDK.
As of this page’s research date, named official coverage of a shipped Steam Workshop catalog, approved mod API, or curated “official mods” list is thin. Do not treat rumor threads as patch notes.

sections.h2: Early Access uncertainty (read this before installing anything)
paragraphs: Steam’s Early Access notes for Sandustry describe ongoing updates — more buildings, resources, production chains, quests, and technologies over a planned EA window on the order of about one year.
Any unofficial file that touches game binaries, saves, or asset packs can break on the next patch. That risk is higher during EA, not lower.
If a download site claims permanent compatibility, free DLC mirrors, or multiplayer “mod modes” without naming a primary Steam news post or official wiki page, treat it as unverified.

sections.h2: Practical first-hour advice instead of chasing packs
paragraphs: If you are new: finish a stable dig → refine → short belt loop in the free demo before hunting mods. Most “I need mods” friction is early logistics pain, not missing Workshop content.
Learn filters, overflow dumps, and wet-sand habits from in-game prompts and the official wiki — those skills transfer even if community mods appear later.
Snapshot saves before any experiment that alters files. Pixel factories are painful to rebuild after a bad install.
Want more systems from the developers? Follow Steam news and the Release Date page on this site for roadmap language — that is the official expansion path during EA.

sections.h2: Where community mod talk actually lives
paragraphs: Official Discord: https://discord.gg/HJNk5eMnmt — best place to see whether developers or moderators acknowledge modding experiments.
Reddit: r/SandustryGame — screenshots and discussion; still not an install authority.
YouTube: @sandustry — trailers and developer-facing video; skim descriptions for any Workshop callouts before trusting a random “top mods” video.
Hooded Horse Sandustry official wiki — use this for game systems; if a modding page appears there later, prefer it over fan mirrors.
Prefer links that originate from Steam, official Discord announcements, or clearly named coverage — not random SEO mirrors.
Avoid “crack,” keygen, or “unlocked multiplayer” packs bundled with factory games; those are malware patterns, not Sandustry features.
Do not paste unknown scripts into your game folder while a save is open.
If something goes wrong, verify game files on Steam and restore a pre-mod save — then re-check Discord for known-good guidance.
Players sometimes confuse mods (third-party or Workshop content) with in-game buildings and production modules.
For machine roles and factory pieces, use this site’s Buildings overview — that page stays role-based and points to the official wiki for patch-sensitive names.
For belt and filter habits without file mods, use Automation Tips.

sections.h2: How this page will stay honest
paragraphs: We will not invent a Workshop URL, a ranked mod list, install paths, or unlock codes.
When Steam news, the official wiki, or developer posts publish concrete modding support, this page should be updated to cite those sources directly.
Until then, the correct SEO answer for sandustry mods is: sources are thin — play the vanilla EA loop, watch official channels, and skip unverified installers.

faq.q: Does Sandustry have Steam Workshop mods?
faq.a: Official preferred sources do not currently give this fan page a solid, citable Workshop catalog to document. Check the live Steam app page and recent Steam news; do not assume Workshop exists because other factory games have it.

faq.q: Is there an official Sandustry modding API?
faq.a: Named official documentation for a public mod API is thin as of this page. Watch the Hooded Horse wiki and developer posts on Discord or Steam — do not trust third-party “API guides” that invent endpoints or folder layouts.

faq.q: Where should I look for Sandustry mod news?
faq.a: Steam news for app 2764460, the official Discord (https://discord.gg/HJNk5eMnmt), r/SandustryGame, @sandustry on YouTube, and the Hooded Horse Sandustry wiki.

faq.q: Are mods safe to install during Early Access?
faq.a: Unofficial mods can break on patches and can risk saves or accounts if the download is shady. Prefer vanilla play until an official channel documents a supported path.

faq.q: I searched mods but I meant buildings — where do I go?
faq.a: Use the Buildings page on this wiki for machine roles, then the official Hooded Horse wiki for exact names and unlocks.

faq.q: Should I buy Early Access just for mods?
faq.a: No. Buy for the dig–refine–automate loop after trying the free demo. Mod support, if it arrives, should be confirmed on Steam — not assumed from search results.
